evidence.1_content: Read in full or near-full: foundations/claude-code/hooks-automation, foundations/claude-code/autonomy-at-scale (source), foundations/math-ml-core/transformers-attention, foundations/mental-models/models-and-effort, foundations/mental-models/what-is-an-llm (source), foundations/chat-assistants/big-three-compared (source), foundations/obsidian/ai-inside-obsidian (source), foundations/workflows-agents/first-automation, applications/agency-freelance/pricing-ai-work, applications/ai-in-companies/governance-security (source). Technical claims I could check are right: hook exit code 2 blocks and feeds stderr back, PreToolUse permissionDecision deny, stop_hook_active loop guard; prefill vs decode, KV cache and prompt caching explained correctly with a worked 4,000-token example; `ollama run gemma4:e2b --verbose` is a real current tag (checked ollama.com/library/gemma4/tags); Play Console 12-tester/14-day rule and Apple $99 / Play $25 fees are correct; EU AI Act Art. 50 date is hedged with 'check for later amendments'. Content avoids brittle model IDs (only a handful in the whole corpus, each labelled as older where relevant, e.g. mobile-apps-with-ai notes the video runs on Opus 4). Each breakdown has a worked example and a 'common failure modes' list; no filler. Gaps: a few primaries are weaker than the writing around them. big-three-compared's video is from a small channel (BitBiasedAI) whose title the lesson itself calls 'buying-guide clickbait'. pricing-ai-work's primary is a 73-minute 2023 design-pricing talk (The Futur) that the learner has to transfer to AI work on their own. ai-inside-obsidian says 'The video is 25.7 minutes against a 14-minute lesson' (an odd decimal).
evidence.2_relevance: No author-specific content found. A content grep for private names, local paths, TODO and internal notes turned up only legitimate teaching uses ('[PLACEHOLDER]' as a technique, 'TODO' as an example of volatile context), and `node scripts/check-public.js` reports 0 errors and 20 warnings, all generic on inspection (Supabase Edge Functions, Flutter/Dart, Play testers, MEMORY.md as a Claude Code feature). Apply-it blocks give branches for each audience ('If you build software:', 'At work or school:', 'No coding project yet? Run the same sort on a checklist you follow at work or in class', 'If you already have a client… If you don't: use a realistic hypothetical client'). Toolkit blocks name ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini equivalents side by side (Projects, Gems, Custom GPTs), and Claude Code lessons name Cursor, Codex, Copilot and git pre-commit fallbacks. The author's name appears only where it should (About, footer, JSON-LD author). One soft spot: 'Get Hired' is a hero CTA on the home page and a top-nav item, but /get-hired serves only one career (Applied AI Engineer). The non-coding professional the home page also addresses gets no equivalent page.
evidence.3_learning_design: Strong spine: the same 8-block anatomy everywhere, 'DO THESE FIRST' prerequisite links in lesson headers (e.g. transformers-attention lists linear algebra, probability, neural networks; the breakdown repeats 'You need: …'), IN PILLAR n/N, pillar pages with 'YOU'LL NEED' (applied-ai-engineering asks for basic Python/JS, a terminal and a spending limit), modules ('Core engineering' / 'Job-ready extras'), three goal routes on Start Here and /path, and prev/next on every lesson. Practice works: recall-first recap cards with a missed-card replay, scenario self-checks with I got it / I missed it grading, and Math & ML MCQs that test judgement rather than arithmetic (transformers Q1/Q5). Gaps: (a) time load. The very first lesson behind 'BEGIN WITH' (what-is-an-llm) shows 94 min, Pillar 6 is ≈23 h, and several lessons exceed 100 min (calling-an-llm-api 113, structured-outputs 116, capstone 152), which is a lot for the stated near-beginner on-ramp. (b) Self-checks in non-math lessons are reveal-and-self-grade only, and some are recall questions ('What are the four repeating steps…' in first-automation). (c) 'Upgrade your AI setup' sometimes holds items that aren't about an AI setup (first-automation: 'Build it on a real signal, not a demo', 'Keep an automation log as a spreadsheet template').
evidence.4_onboarding: Home makes it clear within seconds: the H1 'Learn AI and AI tools, one studied lesson at a time', a subline naming all three audiences, 'FREE · NO SIGN-UP' trust points, a 'Pick your route' block with three goal routes, and an 8-step 'How every lesson works' strip. Start Here repeats the routes, sets session expectations ('Most fit one sitting of 40–90 minutes') and gives one filled CTA, 'BEGIN WITH: WHAT AN LLM ACTUALLY IS'. Small friction: on desktop the first thing in the sheet is a stats title-block (SECTIONS 2 / PILLARS 12 / LESSONS 111 / DONE) that sits above the value proposition, and the first recommended lesson is 94 min (an 8-minute 3Blue1Brown alternative is offered, but only inside the lesson).
evidence.5_navigation: Top nav (Start Here, Foundations, Applications, Get Hired, Progress, Search, About); mobile Menu button with aria-expanded and aria-controls that closes on Escape. Lessons have a 'Course contents' sidebar on desktop, an 'On this page' jump nav, breadcrumb pillar link, BACK TO PILLAR and PREVIOUS/NEXT LESSON. Cross-lesson '→' pointers render as titled links (models-and-effort → 'The big three compared', 'Choosing models & providers (build-time)'). Search is good: typo-tolerant ('retreival' finds RAG fundamentals first), ranks 'prompt caching' to Cost, latency & caching, has level filters with aria-pressed, keeps state in the URL (?q=mcp&level=advanced), and shows a helpful zero-results message. Nits: models-and-effort ends a pointer with '→ the chat-assistants pillar', where the slug is left as plain, unlinked text. /path opens with no goal selected but still shows the four tracks in an order (Building products first) that matches none of the goals until you pick one.
evidence.6_interactive: Everything tested works. Recap: Start → Flip → I had it / Not yet across 7 cards, a 'You recalled 5 of 7' summary with 'Go over the 2 you missed' and 'Replay all', and focus moves to the next action. Self-check reveal toggles aria-expanded with aria-controls, then offers I got it / I missed it. Challenge quiz (transformers-attention): commit an answer, it locks (aria-disabled), marks '(your pick) ✗' and '(correct answer) ✓', explains in an aria-live region and persists the best score ('Best so far: 4/5'). Mark complete becomes 'COMPLETED' (aria-pressed=true) and survives a reload, and so does the note ('test note round 8'). The dashboard updates rank, XP, streak, badges and per-pillar counts, and Continue points to the next unfinished lesson. Get Hired phases are an accordion with 8 checklist items, a readiness % and a time-to-ready estimate. Export/Import/Erase exist (source reviewed: Erase is confirm-gated and Import validates the `ai-learn:` prefix; I didn't trigger a download). Nits: Import merges into existing data with no preview or confirmation, so importing an old backup silently overwrites the current progress key. The 'Bullseye: ace a self-check' badge depends on self-grading, so it's easy to game.
evidence.7_visual: A distinctive 'graph-paper sheet' look: an indigo-ink pad with a ruled grid, condensed Archivo labels, Atkinson Hyperlegible prose and ruled field boxes. It's coherent across home, lessons, dashboard and Get Hired, and nothing like a template. Prose measures well for long reading: 17px Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, 27px line height, about 660–700px measure (≈70–78ch) at 1280. Hierarchy is clear (numbered section boxes 1–10 per lesson, H2/H3 structure, Try-it callouts, copy-able prompt cards, ASCII pipeline diagrams). The in-app screenshot tool mostly timed out in this environment, so I judged the visuals from one rendered screenshot plus computed styles. Minor: lesson H1s render as 'Title : Subtitle' with the colon on its own line in text extraction; the uppercase labels are dense where many stack (header cells LEVEL/TIME/REVIEWED/IN PILLAR); and some lesson bodies are long walls of text with only ASCII diagrams and no images.
evidence.8_mobile: No horizontal scroll at 320px on 13 pages tested (home, start-here, foundations, a pillar, 3 lessons, search, dashboard, get-hired, path, about, 404): scrollWidth equals clientWidth on each. The in-app pane actually ran at 269px and still had no page overflow; wide code blocks scroll inside their own container. No text under 12px anywhere. The only interactive elements under 24px tall are inline prose links (exempt) and the 'DO THESE FIRST' prerequisite links (20px tall, separated by ' · '), which are a little tight to tap.
evidence.9_accessibility: A skip link is the first focusable element; main has id=main; html lang=en; landmarks are labelled (Main, On this page, Lesson navigation, Course contents); the heading outline is sensible (one H1, H2 per block, H3 inside the breakdown); there are no img elements without alt. Disclosure buttons use aria-expanded/aria-controls; filters and mark-complete use aria-pressed; quiz feedback is aria-live; the notes textarea is labelled 'Your notes'; the search input is labelled; :focus-visible draws a 2px print-colour outline; prefers-reduced-motion is handled in globals.css. Contrast from the tokens on the sheet (#e5eaf6): print 8.3:1, muted 6.2:1, graphite 12:1, pencil 8.4:1, red-pen 4.65:1. Nits: red-pen text (#c0341d) falls to about 4.3:1 on the tinted panels (--tint), below 4.5:1 for normal text if used there (e.g. ✗ marks, the Erase all button on a tinted box). The visually hidden file input on /dashboard (sr-only, not tabindex=-1) leaves an invisible tab stop after 'Import progress'. Quiz options are plain buttons with no group semantics (no role=radiogroup/fieldset with a legend tying them to the question).
evidence.10_trust: Every lesson credits the creator and year under the video ('— 3Blue1Brown · 2024'), carries a 'Why this one' that names weaknesses honestly (big-three: 'buying-guide clickbait… treat the verdicts as one person's impressions'; ai-inside-obsidian: 'sponsored by Smart Connections… you're watching an advocate') and Watch notes on what has aged. I checked all 111 primary videos with YouTube oEmbed: 111/111 return 200, and every author_name matches the claimed channel. About states that lessons were 'drafted with AI assistance and checked against the sources', explains what a Reviewed date covers, says why 106 lessons share 3 Oct 2026, and gives the privacy model (no accounts, cookies or analytics; YouTube loads only on press-to-play via youtube-nocookie). The weekly link re-check it claims is real (.github/workflows/check.yml runs check-links on a Monday cron). There's a 'Report it on GitHub' link on every lesson and a 'What changed in the last review' note. The pricing lesson labels its numbers as illustrative and hypothetical. No hype found.
evidence.11_technical: All routes return 200 in 3–30 ms; unknown URLs return a real 404 with noindex and a helpful page (search + Start Here). Per-lesson metadata is complete: unique title and description, canonical, og:* and twitter:* with a per-lesson 1200×630 opengraph-image, LearningResource JSON-LD with timeRequired, dateModified, isAccessibleForFree and an embedded VideoObject, plus robots.txt and sitemap.xml. No console errors on a clean lesson load (the 404s in the log came from my own made-up URLs). The repo's own read-only link gate (node scripts/check-links.js) passed all 253 videos (primary plus backup) and 171 of 175 external links. Its 4 'failures' are the known Cloudflare connection timeouts (simonwillison.net, eugeneyan.com, r2d3.us, consc.net), so I count them as couldn't-verify, not dead. The 9 warnings are 403 bot blocks (OpenAI help, Make, Perplexity, Midjourney, Medium). The YouTube facade defers the player. Nits: the JSON-LD VideoObject lacks uploadDate (Google requires it for video rich results, and the year is already in frontmatter) and a duration. The public repo tracks docs/review/round-*.json and REVIEWER-BRIEF.md, so the review process ships with the source; that's fine if intended, but it's a leftover-of-process to decide on before publishing.

fixes.issue: A few primary videos are weaker than the lesson around them: one is from a small channel with a clickbait title the lesson has to apologise for, and one is a 73-minute, 2023 design-pricing talk the learner must translate to AI work themselves.
fixes.fix: Re-run the video search for these two and prefer a primary whose 'why' doesn't need a disclaimer, e.g. a criteria-based 2026 comparison from an established reviewer, and a shorter value-pricing talk aimed at services or AI freelancers. Or keep the long Futur talk and add timestamped 'watch these ranges' notes, as ai-inside-obsidian already does.

fixes.issue: Time load is heavy for a near-beginner on-ramp: the 'BEGIN WITH' lesson shows 94 min, several lessons exceed 100 min, and Pillar 6 totals about 23 h, so first sessions risk feeling like a slog.
fixes.fix: In lessons over 90 min, add a 'Short path (≈40 min)' line under the header naming what to do first (e.g. the 8-min 3Blue1Brown video + breakdown + task) and what to come back to. Split the 150-min capstone into two parts with their own completion marks.

fixes.issue: Outside Math & ML and the career lessons, self-checks are reveal-only, and some are pure recall. The 'Upgrade your AI setup' block sometimes contains general workflow tips rather than AI-setup changes.
fixes.where: /foundations/workflows-agents/first-automation (self-check Q1 'What are the four repeating steps'; toolkit bullets 'Build it on a real signal', 'Keep an automation log')
fixes.fix: Swap recall questions for short scenario questions, add 2–3 committed MCQs to each pillar's capstone or hardest lesson, and move non-AI-setup tips from the toolkit into the breakdown or the task.

fixes.issue: 'Get Hired' is a hero CTA and top-nav item, but the page serves only Applied AI Engineer job seekers, so a non-coding professional who clicks it lands on a developer roadmap.
fixes.fix: Relabel the CTA 'Get hired as an AI engineer', or add a one-line note at the top of /get-hired pointing professionals to Track C / Track D (e.g. 'Not aiming for an engineering role? Use AI in your current job → Track C').

fixes.issue: One pointer is left as an unlinked slug, and /path shows a track order before any goal is chosen.
fixes.fix: Link the pillar by name ('Chat assistants: use them like a pro'), and have check-public flag '→ the <slug> pillar' patterns. On /path, preselect the goal saved in the URL or localStorage, or show a 'pick a goal to order the tracks' prompt instead of an unexplained default order.

fixes.issue: Import progress silently merges and overwrites the current progress with whatever is in the file. There is no preview or undo.
fixes.fix: Before writing, show 'This file has N completed lessons from <date>; you currently have M. Replace / Cancel' via confirm(), and keep a one-step undo by stashing the previous values under an ai-learn:backup key.

fixes.issue: Red-pen text is about 4.3:1 on tinted panels. The hidden file input is an invisible tab stop. Quiz options have no grouping semantics.
fixes.where: --red-pen on --tint; /dashboard file input; McqQuiz option lists
fixes.fix: Darken --red-pen slightly (e.g. #b02e18, about 5:1 on tint) or keep red text off tinted fills. Add tabIndex={-1} to the sr-only file input. Wrap each question's options in role='group' (or fieldset) with aria-labelledby pointing at the question text.

fixes.issue: The JSON-LD VideoObject lacks uploadDate and duration, so it is ineligible for video rich results. Review-process files are tracked in the public repo.
fixes.fix: Emit uploadDate (from video.year, or better, the exact publish date via oEmbed or the Data API) and duration (ISO 8601 from video.minutes). Decide deliberately whether docs/review/ ships, and gitignore it if not.

verdict: A genuinely strong, honest course: accurate and current teaching, worked examples and failure modes in every lesson, 111/111 primary videos verified live and correctly attributed, and practice and progress features that all work, with no private leftovers in the content. What holds it at 'excellent with nits' rather than best-in-class is mostly weight and polish: very long lessons for a near-beginner on-ramp, a couple of primary videos weaker than the writing around them, and small navigation, accessibility and metadata nits.
